docs.title: OHDSI Prompt Registry
docs.text:
Use the registry to find reusable guidance for a task and give your agent a shared way to approach it. A prompt pack brings together instructions and, where useful, examples, structured contracts, and review formats.

For example, a research-question pack can help a team turn a study idea into an explicit question. A concept-grounding pack can guide the evidence needed for a mapping decision. The registry makes these packs available through Groundworkers; your agent carries out the conversation and uses the available tools.

flowchart TD
    accTitle: How a prompt pack supports a task
    accDescr: The agent and its draft result sit inside the agentive framework, with the human and prompt pack outside it. Core instructions guide the task, explanations are read as needed, and schemas check structured outputs when provided.
    subgraph PACK["Pack selected from the registry"]
        CORE["Core instructions"]
        EXTRA["Explanations and examples"]
        SCHEMA["Schemas, when provided"]
    end
    subgraph FRAMEWORK["Agentive framework"]
        AGENT["Agent<br/>Conversation and domain tools"]
        AGENT --> RESULT["Draft or decision<br/>for your review"]
    end
    USER["Human in the loop<br/>Goal and context"] <-->|Questions and answers| AGENT
    CORE -->|Guide the task| AGENT
    EXTRA -. Read as needed .-> AGENT
    SCHEMA -. Check structured output .-> RESULT

docs.title: Choose guidance by the decision you need to make
docs.text:
Start with your goal, the setting, and the result you need. Ask your agent to find a suitable pack and explain its scope before applying it:

Find a prompt pack to help us turn our study idea into a research question. Show us which decisions it covers and what information we need to supply.

The catalogue describes the packs available in your Groundworkers installation. Availability depends on your installed content and local configuration. A pack's scope matters more than a familiar name: guidance for one study setting may need different assumptions from guidance for another.

Different packs can contribute different parts of the work:

Need Role of the guidance Decide what happens next Workflow guidance identifies prerequisites, open decisions, and dependent outputs. Clarify something with a person User elicitation asks a focused question and records the answer or unresolved point. Make a domain decision Domain guidance supplies relevant rules, evidence requirements, and review criteria. Pass a result to another tool or team A structured contract defines the information the next consumer expects.

A workflow can use elicitation when it needs an answer. Elicitation is also useful on its own. Domain rules remain relevant whichever conversation format is used.

docs.title: Work with a pack
docs.text:
1. Agree the scope. Explain your goal, known constraints, and intended output. Check that the selected pack fits.
  2. Resolve the necessary decisions. Let the agent use information already supplied and ask about material gaps. State uncertainty rather than choosing an answer you cannot support.
  3. Review the result. Check assumptions, unresolved questions, and evidence before using an output in further work.

You can ask for a different explanation style or more background without changing the underlying decision. You can also correct an earlier answer; the agent should identify which dependent results need review.

docs.title: Read deeper when it helps
docs.text:
Core instructions tell the agent what it needs for the task. Orientation, rationale, and longer examples can be separate references, available when an unfamiliar topic or difficult decision needs explanation.

The registry's selected-content tool reads one declared item at a time. It returns links to other material without fetching their bodies. This supports focused context use; the client or agent still decides which references to request.

docs.title: Understand what validation tells you
docs.text:
Some packs use JSON Schemas to check structured inputs and results. These checks help tools agree on fields and permitted values. Other guidance primarily shapes a decision or conversation and does not need a JSON result.

A structurally valid answer still needs the relevant scientific, clinical, or operational review. An answer to a clarification question also needs to be distinguished from approval to perform an action. The registry publishes guidance and checks contracts; the calling application or agent manages execution and session state.

docs.title: Find the right guide
docs.text:
For a study-design task, start with Working on a research question.

  • Questions and workflow decisions: how clarification, uncertainty, and changed answers fit into work.
  • Choosing and configuring pack sources: shared content, local customisation, and overrides.
  • Authoring a prompt pack: scope, core instructions, optional explanations, and contracts.
  • Tools and structured handoffs: exact calls, validation behaviour, and retrieval limits.
  • Development and Python API reference: maintaining or embedding the registry.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: Use this guide when changing the registry implementation or contributing content to its distribution. For writing a standalone pack, start with Authoring a prompt pack.

docs.title: Local checks
docs.text:
uv sync --all-extras --dev
uv run ruff check .
uv run ty check src/
uv run pytest -q

The registry caches the discovered set for the process lifetime and reads declared document and schema contents on demand. Restart the host after changing pack directories, manifests, or entry-point installations.

docs.title: Research-question contracts
docs.text:
The research pack provides two ordinary JSON Schemas. study-intent.schema.json accepts drafts; study-intent-final.schema.json defines a complete artifact, including template/analytics pairing, required parameters, meaningful values, and permitted nulls. The generic validation and rendering tools use the selected schema. The final schema is maintained by hand; no generator or research-specific Python validator is needed.

catalogue.yaml supplies question guidance and the renderer's parameter rows. Template requirements appear in both the catalogue and the final schema. The author checks in tests/test_research_pilot.py compare their template coverage, pairing, required/nullable fields, and unused-field rules. They also verify that copied draft definitions are unchanged and that the two renderers differ only in their schema and null display text.

When changing a template, update both files and run the tests. Override-pack authors own the same consistency checks: runtime schema validation does not compare the catalogue with the schema. A catalogue-only edit changes guidance and review rows without changing what passes validation. Keep the files consistent while the host uses them; on-demand reads do not provide an atomic update across files. Check status after installing an override, since a rejected pack may leave a lower-precedence copy active.

Paired elicitation validation remains a separate capability: ohdsi_prompt_registry_validate_elicitation checks correlation and answer policy that the individual request/result schemas cannot establish alone. Neither artifact validation nor pair validation proves user agreement, scientific suitability, or active workflow state. Native/text/batch adherence needs client evaluation.

The development helpers in evaluation/ exercise an isolated registry host and installed package. They keep model conversations separate from deterministic tests. Use evaluation/README.md for the synthetic scenarios, trace collection, and rollback procedure. A successful headless question exchange establishes protocol behavior; check presentation with real users in each supported client before claiming UI compatibility.

docs.title: Serving the documentation locally
docs.text: uv run mkdocs serve

docs.title: Versioning and releases
docs.text:
The version is derived from git tags by hatch-vcs; there is no version string in any source file and there is no CHANGELOG.md. The release history lives in GitHub Releases, drafted by release-drafter as PRs merge.

Every pull request against main must carry exactly one of breaking, feature, fix, dependencies, or chore. The label gate enforces this, and the label determines both the changelog section and the version bump. See the cava-devops PR workflow for the full process.

uv.lock is kept in step with pyproject.toml by a pre-commit hook. Enable it once per clone:

git config core.hooksPath .githooks

docs.title: Groundworkers dependency
docs.text: The registry integrates through the Groundworkers plugin interface. Its declared dependency is groundworkers[tui]>=0.7,<1; use the dependency constraints in pyproject.toml when preparing a compatible environment. Install the registry and content distributions into the environment that runs the host, and restart it after changing plugin or pack registration.

docs.title: Questions and workflow decisions
docs.text:
Use user elicitation when an agent needs to understand something from a person. Use workflow management when it needs to coordinate decisions and the outputs that depend on them. These capabilities can work together, but either can be useful independently.

The user-elicitation and workflow-management packs provide shared instructions for these responsibilities. A domain pack supplies the study-specific or mapping-specific rules that determine whether a decision is suitable for the work.

docs.title: A question gathers information
docs.text:
A useful question explains what needs to be decided and gives enough context to answer it. It asks about a material gap rather than repeating information already supplied. Where a choice is useful, the options should have clear meanings; where the answer cannot be anticipated, a text question is more appropriate.

For example:

Which population should this research question describe: adults with a new diagnosis, adults with an existing diagnosis, or a population you would like to describe in your own words?

Collecting that answer does not require a complete study workflow. It may be a standalone clarification. Within a workflow, the same answer can resolve one decision while other decisions remain open.

docs.title: A workflow decides what can progress
docs.text:
A workflow relates the goal to prerequisites, decisions, and dependent artifacts. It needs to distinguish an answer that has been understood from a decision that satisfies the relevant domain rules.

For example, a team may clearly describe a target population while still needing to assess whether the available data can identify it. The clarification is answered; the feasibility decision remains open. A dependent cohort definition needs that distinction to be visible.

The workflow-management pack describes how to represent this context. The calling application or agent must maintain it and apply the prerequisites. Publishing or validating a workflow document does not execute the workflow or enforce its dependencies.

docs.title: An unanswered question is a meaningful result
docs.text:
The elicitation contract distinguishes four outcomes:

Outcome Meaning Answered The user's response has been understood in the requested form. Deferred The user explicitly wants to answer later. Declined The user explicitly chooses not to answer. Unresolved There is no usable answer, including an interrupted interaction without an explicit disposition.

An unanswered dialog does not establish refusal, consent, or a default answer. While a question is waiting for a response, its pending state belongs to the application hosting the conversation.

If a required decision remains unresolved, the workflow should show what depends on it. Work that does not need that decision can continue where the workflow permits it.

docs.title: Changing an answer can change dependent work
docs.text:
Suppose a team changes its population from all adults to people with a new diagnosis. The revised answer may affect the research question, cohort definition, and feasibility assessment.

The agent should associate the reply with the question it answers, recognise which revision is current, and identify dependent outputs that need review. A reply to an earlier version of a question should not silently replace a later decision. The host is responsible for retaining this state and preventing a reply from being applied twice.

The request/result contract supports this with question identity and revision fields. These fields help correlate a reply; they do not themselves establish which revision is active or whether the science is sound.

docs.title: The presentation depends on your client
docs.text:
An agent should use a native question control when the host exposes and permits one. Otherwise, a clear text question can carry the same meaning. Native tool names and capabilities vary between clients; installing a prompt pack does not create a question dialog or guarantee that an external agent follows the guidance.

You can request concise questions, explanations of unfamiliar terms, or more background. A client running without a person available should leave requests unresolved rather than inventing user answers. Agents should not switch execution modes just to obtain a dialog.

docs.title: Keep explanations available without loading everything
docs.text:
The core pack instructions contain the behaviour needed for routine use. Optional references explain orientation, changed answers, presentation choices, and examples. An agent starting with little context can request the relevant explanation; a routine interaction can use the core alone.

Separate references make selective reading possible. The registry does not fetch their bodies with the core instructions, although a client can choose to request them. Essential rules therefore belong in the core, and reference descriptions should say when deeper reading is useful.

docs.title: Review before using an answer
docs.text:
Contract validation can check the shape of a request/result pair, matching identities and revisions, and whether an answer follows the offered choices or free-text policy. It cannot establish that a person really supplied the answer, that it is the latest reply, or that it meets domain requirements.

Treat “answered,” “suitable for the study,” and “approved to execute” as separate judgements. The domain workflow and host determine what further checks or permissions are required.

For exact retrieval calls, schemas, and validation interfaces, see Tools and structured handoffs.

docs.title: Authoring a prompt pack
docs.text: Build a pack around a defined responsibility: a task to guide, a decision to clarify, or a structured handoff to support. All pack sources use the same manifest contract.

docs.title: Start with scope and boundaries
docs.text:
Describe when the pack is useful, what information it needs, and what result it helps produce. State which domain judgements belong to the caller. A generic questioning capability, for example, can establish that an answer is understood while leaving study feasibility to the domain workflow.

Keep responsibilities separable. A workflow can call on elicitation without duplicating its presentation rules. A clarification should also be usable without inventing a workflow around it. Examples should show both a normal result and a meaningful unresolved or review path.

docs.title: Separate instructions from optional explanation
docs.text:
Put essential operational rules in the core instructions. Declare orientation, rationale, and longer examples as separate documents, with descriptions saying when to read them. An unfamiliar agent can request the relevant background while a routine invocation reads only the core.

A declared prompt should select the core document. Selected-content retrieval returns reference metadata without recursively loading document bodies or related packs. Links and see_also entries describe relationships; they are not executable includes.

Essential boundaries must be understandable from the core alone. Optional explanations should expand those boundaries rather than introduce hidden requirements.

docs.title: Use structure where a consumer needs a contract
docs.text:
Use JSON Schema when another tool or service needs to check an input or result. Decision guidance can remain prose when a machine-readable result serves no purpose. A pack can declare schemas: {} and render: {} when it needs neither validation nor rendering.

A schema expresses fields and permitted values. Instructions explain how to make the decision, handle uncertainty, and obtain the necessary evidence. Keep domain suitability, user approval, and contract validity distinct.

docs.title: Declare the pack
docs.text:
This example publishes a review prompt and an input schema:

name: my-site-review
title: Site review workflow
version: "1.0"
shareability: private
scope_summary: Reviews a site-specific analytic request and returns a structured result.

applicability:
  tags: [site-review]

documents:
  instructions:
    path: instructions.md
    mime_type: text/markdown
    description: Core instructions for the review workflow.
  examples:
    path: examples.json
    mime_type: application/json
    description: Read when a normal or unresolved review needs illustration.

schemas:
  request:
    path: request.schema.json
    description: JSON Schema for the review request.

prompts:
  review:
    document: instructions
    title: Run the site review
    description: Review one site request using the declared contract.
    arguments:
      request:
        description: A JSON review request.
        required: false

render: {}
requires_tools: []
tool_prefix: site

The files named in the manifest must exist. The published prompt name is site_review; prompt arguments are strings, including JSON encoded as text.

Field Purpose name, version Stable identity and content version. The name also selects overrides. scope_summary, descriptions Help people and agents choose the pack and its documents. documents Declare readable text or structured resources. schemas Declare JSON Schemas used by validation. prompts Publish selected documents in the MCP prompt list. render Declare optional deterministic Markdown renderers. requires_tools Advertise dependencies; missing tools appear in readiness without disabling discovery. applicability Support discovery by tags. always: true includes the pack in every tag-filtered catalogue query.

The always flag affects catalogue inclusion. It does not automatically load instructions or establish a universal domain rule. Scope and applicability still need to be accurate.

docs.title: Reference a schema from instructions
docs.text:
When a schema is essential to a prompt, use a placeholder rather than maintaining a second copy:

## Input contract

Provide a document conforming to:

{{schema:request}}

The placeholder expands when the document is read. A misspelled or undeclared schema placeholder rejects the pack at load time. Expanded schemas increase the selected content size, so include only essential contracts inline and expose other schemas as separate reads.

docs.title: Separate drafts from complete handoffs
docs.text:
A pack can declare several ordinary schemas and renderers for the same task. The research-question pack, for example, has study_intent for drafts and study_intent_final for complete artifacts. A renderer's schema selects the checks that must pass before it produces Markdown. The generic validate and render tools work with either key.

Write final requirements in the schema, including conditional requirements where a selected template changes the required fields. Keep local $ref targets and static object properties available to renderer integrity checks; the current renderer does not infer paths through arbitrary allOf compositions. The research final schema exposes its analysis $ref beside its conditional allOf rules.

If catalogue data also describes requirements or determines review rows, test that it agrees with the schema. For the research pack, that includes template coverage, analytics pairing, required and nullable fields, and unused-field rules. Also check copied draft definitions and renderer parity. These are author checks; runtime validation uses the schema and does not compare independently edited files. Override authors must maintain their own consistent catalogue/schema pair. A schema-valid artifact can otherwise omit important values from its catalogue-driven review table.

Overrides replace whole packs. If a higher-precedence copy is rejected, an already accepted lower-precedence copy remains active; if no valid copy exists, the pack is unavailable. Inspect ohdsi_prompt_registry_status for rejections and the effective source after installing an override. A shared pack source does not itself guarantee content consistency or atomic file updates. See Pack sources.

Request/result relationships can still need a dedicated capability check. The paired elicitation tool checks matching identity/revision, offered choices, and free-text policy after validating the individual schemas. It does not prove human provenance or determine the caller's active revision.

docs.title: Choose a distribution layout
docs.text:
For a filesystem pack, place the pack directory under a configured root. For bundled content, place it under src/ohdsi_prompt_registry/packs/ and release it with the registry.

A separately distributed pack uses the ohdsi_prompt_registry.packs entry-point group:

[project.entry-points."ohdsi_prompt_registry.packs"]
my_pack = "my_pack.packs"

The target is a package or directory containing direct child pack directories:

src/my_pack/packs/
├── __init__.py
└── my-installed-pack/
    ├── manifest.yaml
    ├── instructions.md
    └── request.schema.json

Include declared content files in the distribution. For configuration and precedence, see Pack sources.

docs.title: Check the pack as a consumer
docs.text:
1. Check that scope and core instructions are sufficient without optional background.
  2. Validate representative structured inputs/results, including unresolved cases where applicable.
  3. Check prompt resolution and selected reads, including schema expansion and content limits.
  4. Restart the host after manifest or discovery changes and verify the effective source in status.
  5. Exercise the intended client: tool availability and presentation behaviour need integration checks beyond schema validation.

The tool reference describes retrieval limits and validation boundaries. The development guide covers repository checks.

Bases: PackageConfigBase

Discovery controls for bundled, installed, and local prompt packs.

docs.title: accept_a_single_root_as_a_string classmethod
docs.text:
accept_a_single_root_as_a_string(value: object) -> object

Keep every configuration written before this field took a list.

One directory was the only option for long enough that config files in the wild spell it as a string, and rewriting them is not something a release should require.

docs.title: Working on a research question
docs.text: Use the research-question pack to turn a study goal into one or more OHDSI analytics templates and a StudyIntent document. Start with the population, comparison, outcome, or follow-up period you already have in mind. The agent should reuse that information and ask about the decisions still open.

docs.title: Choose a flow
docs.text:
The pack provides two prompts:

Prompt Use rqt_structure_question The sequential research-question workflow, with its StudyIntent validation and review format. rqt_structure_question_pilot An opt-in flow that composes shared question-asking and workflow guidance, supports drafts with open questions, and checks a separate final contract.

Choose the pilot explicitly from your client's prompt list. A tool-only client can retrieve its resolved instructions with ohdsi_prompt_registry_get:

{
  "pack": "ohdsi-question-templates",
  "kind": "prompt",
  "key": "structure_question_pilot",
  "arguments": {
    "question": "Help us define the incidence of stroke in adults with type 2 diabetes.",
    "mode": "interactive",
    "presentation": "native_preferred"
  }
}

Arguments are strings. You can also supply a draft and compact workflow context as JSON text to resume work. Keep the decisions and their source information with the draft; a document labelled “accepted” cannot establish what was actually agreed in an earlier conversation.

docs.title: Expect questions about decisions, not formatting
docs.text:
The catalogue defines the supported templates, their analytics types, and the parameters each needs. The agent should explain a choice when it matters, ask one focused question at a time by default, and keep uncertainty visible.

For example, a population and outcome may be clear while the follow-up period remains undecided. The agent can show a draft and ask about that period. It should not invent a duration to make the document pass validation.

The pilot uses native question controls where your client permits them and text otherwise. With mode: "batch", missing answers are returned as unresolved requests alongside the draft. It does not attempt a dialog. Client behaviour still needs checking in the environment where you use it.

docs.title: Distinguish a draft from a complete handoff
docs.text:
Drafts and complete handoffs use different checks:

Purpose Validation and rendering What the checks allow Draft Schema and renderer key study_intent Incomplete analyses and parameters while decisions are open. Complete structure Schema and renderer key study_intent_final At least one analysis, correct template/analytics pairing, and the required parameters.

Use ohdsi_prompt_registry_validate or ohdsi_prompt_registry_render with pack ohdsi-question-templates, the appropriate schema or renderer key, and document as a JSON string. Final rendering checks the final schema before producing Markdown. It rejects unknown fields, blank text, and empty or duplicate treatment-list entries, and requires each relevant parameter to be present.

The final schema permits a null nesting cohort for the two effect-estimation designs. That allowance must reflect a decision, rather than an unanswered question. Unused parameters, including nesting cohorts in other templates, must be omitted or null. They do not appear as meaningful selections in the review table.

The catalogue guides the conversation and supplies the review rows; the final schema determines what passes validation. Pack authors keep these declarations aligned. If you use a local override, changing the catalogue alone does not change the validation rules; see Authoring a prompt pack.

Passing these checks means the structure is complete. It does not establish scientific suitability, human agreement, or permission to execute a study. The agent or calling application must check those matters and keep dependent work pending when required decisions are unresolved.

docs.title: Change an answer without restarting the whole task
docs.text:
Ask the agent to update the affected decisions and drafts. A new follow-up period may change an incidence analysis while leaving a separate characterization analysis intact. An older reply must not overwrite the current answer, and an identical duplicate should not be applied twice.

The caller manages question revisions, dependencies, and saved state. The pilot instructions guide that behaviour; the registry does not provide a session store or enforce what an external agent says in chat.

For a worked case, read the pack's optional pilot_examples document. Routine invocation reads the pilot core; it directs the agent to the shared capability cores and catalogue as needed for the task, without preloading explanations or example collections. See Questions and workflow decisions for the shared interaction model and Tools and structured handoffs for exact validation calls.

docs.title: Choosing and configuring pack sources
docs.text:
Choose a source according to who maintains the guidance and how you want to distribute it. All sources use the same pack format; a source describes where content comes from, rather than what kind of decision it supports.

Source Useful for Precedence Bundled Baseline content released with the registry. Lowest Installed Shared content distributed and versioned separately. Middle Filesystem Site-owned guidance, local development, or an intentional override. Highest 
flowchart TD
    accTitle: How pack sources form the active catalogue
    accDescr: Valid, enabled packs from bundled, installed, and filesystem sources are selected by name. Filesystem takes priority over installed, then bundled. Different names coexist; lower-priority copies of the same name are shadowed, not merged.
    BUNDLED["Bundled<br/>Registry release"] --> SELECT["Choose a copy for each pack name<br/>Filesystem > installed > bundled"]
    INSTALLED["Installed<br/>Content distributions"] --> SELECT
    FILESYSTEM["Filesystem<br/>Local or site-owned directories"] --> SELECT
    SELECT --> ACTIVE["Active catalogue<br/>One effective pack per name"]
    SELECT -.-> SHADOWED["Other copies of the same name<br/>Reported as shadowed"]

Use the catalogue to see available content and ohdsi_prompt_registry_status to check its effective source. Discovery makes guidance available to an agent; it does not establish its clinical authority or make every pack apply to every task.

docs.title: Understand overrides before customising
docs.text:
A pack's manifest name is its identity. If two valid packs have the same name, the higher-precedence source replaces the entire lower-precedence pack. Files from the two copies are not merged. Status reports the shadowed source so a local override is visible.

Use the same name when deliberately replacing an existing contract. Use a different name when offering a separate workflow or alternative approach. Check the effective source after configuration so you know which instructions your team is using.

A malformed pack is rejected independently; sibling packs can still load. Status distinguishes rejection from a valid pack being shadowed.

docs.title: Bundled content
docs.text:
Bundled packs ship inside ohdsi-prompt-registry and are available by default. They include research-question guidance and the generic elicitation and workflow-management capabilities.

[tools.ohdsi_prompt_registry]
include_bundled = true

Choose bundled content when its scope fits your task. A site-specific change can be maintained as a filesystem pack without modifying the registry distribution.

docs.title: Installed content
docs.text:
Installed packs come from separate Python distributions, such as omop-concept-grounding. Install the distribution into the environment running Groundworkers and restart the host so discovery can register its packs.

Installed discovery is enabled by default. An optional allow-list restricts the active set across sources:

[tools.ohdsi_prompt_registry]
include_installed = true
enabled_packs = ["omop-concept-grounding"]

The allow-list uses manifest names, rather than distribution or entry-point names. Inspect the catalogue after installation to see each pack's instructions, resources, and published prompts.

docs.title: Local and site-owned content
docs.text:
Use filesystem packs for local guidance or a working copy of shared content. Set packs_root to a directory whose direct children are packs:

[tools.ohdsi_prompt_registry]
packs_root = "./prompt-packs"
include_bundled = true
include_installed = true

A typical layout is:

prompt-packs/
└── my-site-review/
    ├── manifest.yaml
    ├── instructions.md
    └── request.schema.json

Relative paths are anchored to the configuration file when Groundworkers supplies OA_CONFIG_PATH. Use an absolute path for an unambiguous standalone launch.

Set packs_root in the configuration file; the setup console does not expose that field. An existing value is preserved when other fields are edited through the console.

docs.title: Shared and personal roots
docs.text:
To keep shared guidance alongside personal working copies, supply roots in ascending precedence:

[tools.ohdsi_prompt_registry]
packs_root = ["/srv/shared/prompt-packs", "~/work/my-packs"]

A pack in the later directory replaces a pack of the same name in an earlier directory, as well as installed or bundled copies. A single root can be supplied as a string. Each root is resolved independently; an unavailable root produces a warning without preventing the others from loading.

To use only a known local set:

[tools.ohdsi_prompt_registry]
packs_root = "/srv/groundcrew/prompt-packs"
include_bundled = false
include_installed = false
enabled_packs = ["my-site-review"]

docs.title: Make configuration changes visible
docs.text:
Restart Groundworkers after adding or removing pack directories, changing manifests, or installing content distributions. The host retains its discovered pack set for the process lifetime. Files already declared by an active pack are read on demand, so editing their contents does not require repackaging.

After a restart, inspect status and retrieve the intended instructions. Confirm the effective source, version, and content identity, especially when resuming work or testing an override. Editing source files alone does not restart a running host.

For the content contract and distribution layout, see Authoring a prompt pack.

docs.title: Tools and structured handoffs
docs.text: This reference is for people configuring an agent or integrating a client. For the user-facing model, start with the overview and Questions and workflow decisions.

docs.title: Discover and select a pack
docs.text:
Call ohdsi_prompt_registry_catalogue with {} to list active packs, or filter by tags:

{"tags": ["concept-mapping"]}

Catalogue entries describe scope, source, documents, schemas, prompts, renderers, and advertised tool dependencies. Use ohdsi_prompt_registry_links with a pack name for its full resource index:

{"pack": "user-elicitation"}

Use ohdsi_prompt_registry_status to diagnose rejected packs, overrides, or missing tool dependencies. A dependency warning describes readiness; it does not remove the pack from discovery.

docs.title: Read selected content
docs.text:
Resource-capable clients can read declared resource URIs. Tool-only clients can use ohdsi_prompt_registry_get to retrieve actual content. Its default selection is the pack's core instructions:

{"pack": "user-elicitation"}

Read one optional document by its declared key:

{"pack": "user-elicitation", "key": "orientation"}

The elicitation pack also declares answer_changes, client_adapters, and examples. These references are linked in routine retrieval; their bodies require explicit reads. There is no recursive loading of references or related packs.

Select a machine contract with kind: "schema":

{"pack": "user-elicitation", "kind": "schema", "key": "request"}

Select a resolved prompt with kind: "prompt":

{"pack": "user-elicitation", "kind": "prompt", "key": "elicit"}

An optional arguments object is permitted only for prompt reads. Its values are strings, including JSON inputs encoded as JSON text. Do not pass arguments on document or schema reads, even as {}. Unknown kinds, undeclared keys, and unknown arguments fail visibly. Selection uses declared pack keys; there is no filesystem-path parameter.

docs.title: Content identity and completeness
docs.text:
Responses include the effective pack version/source, MIME type, UTF-8 content size, SHA-256 content identity, complete, content, and at most ten reference links. references_omitted counts further index entries; use the catalogue or links tool for the full index.

Content identity covers the resolved text, including invocation arguments, or canonical compact JSON for structured content. Retain effective version/source and content identity with saved work so a resumed task can detect a different instruction set.

The selected-content JSON envelope is capped at 65,536 UTF-8 bytes, before MCP transport encoding and overhead. Oversized responses contain complete: false, content: null, and CONTENT_TOO_LARGE. Do not treat that response as partial instructions. A resource-capable client can read the declared resource; authors can split long material into smaller declared documents. There is no implicit pagination or silent truncation.

Declared file contents are read on demand. Changing the discovered pack set or manifests requires a host restart; see Pack sources.

docs.title: Invoke a published prompt
docs.text:
Declared prompts appear in the MCP prompt list as <tool_prefix>_<prompt key>. Bundled examples are rqt_structure_question, ue_elicit, and wm_coordinate. Other prompts depend on the installed and configured packs.

For the opt-in rqt_structure_question_pilot prompt and its draft/final contract checks, see Working on a research question.

For example, invoke rqt_structure_question with:

{"question": "Does semaglutide reduce cardiovascular risk?"}

Native prompt invocation and selected prompt retrieval expose instructions for the consuming agent. They do not run a model or persist a conversation themselves.

docs.title: Validate a document or an answer pair
docs.text:
ohdsi_prompt_registry_validate checks one JSON document against a named schema in the effective pack. Pass pack, schema, and document; document is a JSON string. Schema validation checks the contract's shape and constraints, not domain correctness.

ohdsi_prompt_registry_validate_elicitation accepts request and result as JSON strings. It validates them against the effective user-elicitation schemas and checks their relationship:

  • Matching request identity and revision.
  • Unique offered choice IDs and answers drawn from the offered choices.
  • Text answers consistent with the request's free-text policy.

Read the pack's declared examples document for valid text, choice, outside-choice text, deferred, cancelled, and revised request/result pairs. For Python consumers, the equivalent helper is ohdsi_prompt_registry.elicitation.validate_elicitation_response(service, request, result).

docs.title: Elicitation contract
docs.text:
The v1 request includes a goal, request_id, positive integer revision, and an answer specification. Supported answer forms are text and single_choice. Choice requests declare option IDs, labels, and whether free text is permitted. Context and interaction policy are optional. A standalone request needs no workflow ID.

Results preserve identity and revision, identify user/none provenance, and contain an answer or a non-answer reason. Outcomes are answered, deferred, declined, and unresolved. Pending interaction state belongs to the host. Cancellation without an explicit user disposition is unresolved.

Overrides of the generic v1 contracts must preserve their semantics. The validator cannot determine the active revision, establish human provenance, detect a previously applied reply, or assess scientific validity. The host owns those checks and storage.

docs.title: Workflow context contract
docs.text:
The workflow-management pack publishes a context schema for phase, resolved decisions and their domain-validation status, pending request-to-decision associations, artifact dependencies/status, and effective pack identity.

Validation does not execute dependencies or prove readiness. A controlled consumer must enforce prerequisites. Adherence by an external agent needs evaluation in the intended client, including native-question and text presentation paths.

docs.title: Render for review
docs.text: ohdsi_prompt_registry_render validates a structured document and uses a pack's declared deterministic renderer to turn it into Markdown for human review. Pass pack, the declared render key, and document as a JSON string; format defaults to "markdown". Rendering is optional: a pack may publish guidance or schemas without a renderer. A rendered document still needs the appropriate review before operational use.

docs.title: Check a complete research intent
docs.text:
Use the generic validation tool with the final research schema:

{
  "pack": "ohdsi-question-templates",
  "schema": "study_intent_final",
  "document": "{\"analyses\":[{\"analytics_type\":\"characterization\",\"template_name\":\"patient_characterization\",\"parameters\":{\"target_cohort\":\"Adults with type 2 diabetes\"}}]}"
}

For Markdown review, call ohdsi_prompt_registry_render with the same pack/document and render: "study_intent_final". It applies that renderer's final schema and returns validation errors instead of Markdown for an invalid document. Both tools retain their existing signatures and error envelopes. Python callers use service.validate(pack, "study_intent_final", document) and service.render(pack, "study_intent_final", document).

The final schema rejects empty analyses, unknown fields, incorrect template/analytics pairing, missing required values, blank text, invalid treatment lists, and nonapplicable values. Permitted nesting nulls appear as intentional in the final review table; the caller must establish that intention from actual decisions. Unused null fields remain allowed and are omitted from the table.

For drafts, use schema/render key study_intent. Draft success does not establish completeness. The catalogue controls guidance and review rows, while the final schema controls validation; authors of bundled and override packs must keep them consistent. Scientific suitability, agreement, and workflow readiness remain caller responsibilities.

docs.title: Check the host integration
docs.text:
After installing packs or changing their manifests, restart Groundworkers to rebuild registration. Inspect status, retrieve the expected instructions, and check the effective source and content identity.

Clients should use native question tools only when exposed and permitted by the host, with text fallback where appropriate. Noninteractive callers leave unanswered requests unresolved. Avoid an additional model call solely to format a question, and do not preload optional reference collections.
